lines.en: A meteor shower was pouring across the pitch-black night sky. It was a sight anyone would have marveled at, but not Yoo Joonghyuk.
「So it's about to begin.」
Because the meteor shower heralded the start of the third main scenario. Now Seoul would fall to ruin, step by step, according to the scenario's prescribed sequence.
Yoo Joonghyuk lowered his gaze from the sky and looked toward the mouth of the Han River.
With the hordes of ichthyosaurs having moved downstream not long ago, the area around Dongho Bridge was fairly quiet and deserted.
「Was it too much to ask after all?」

It had already been three days since that fellow Kim Dokja had gone into the Han River. Asking someone who had only just cleared the first main scenario to kill an ichthyosaur might have been asking too much.
「Well, even I'd have trouble killing an ichthyosaur in 3 days.」
But he thought taking Kim Dokja along would be impossible unless Dokja was capable of at least that much. If Dokja couldn't even manage that, he would only get in the way.
「A prophet, was he? He wasn't much after all.」
Yoo Joonghyuk closed his eyes, disappointment on his face. He would go on alone again. Without a single companion.
It was nothing particularly remarkable.
He had been alone all along.
「This time, I'll change it for certain.」
And so Yoo Joonghyuk turned away.
But perhaps he had turned away too soon.
[W-what is it?]
I blinked over and over, but all I could see was a grayish-white ceiling. I was still inside the ichthyosaur. When I turned my head, I found Bihyung staring wide-eyed in alarm.
“······I had a dream.”
[Oho, planting some foreshadowing to pique their curiosity, are you? You're pretty good at this!]
That wasn't it, but I figured it didn't really matter if he misunderstood.
[A few constellations want you to move to a new location quickly.]
I had just used ‘Ellain Forest’s Vital Force,’ which I'd bought from Bihyung for 500 coins, and fallen asleep. I'd judged that moving around while exhausted would be dangerous.
Ellain Forest’s Vital Force forces you into a deep sleep for 2 hours, but rapidly relieves fatigue and heals wounds throughout your body in return.
In other words, the item was worth its steep price.
“······Shall I head out for real now?”
Muttering something suitable to myself, I stretched my stiff body.
The dream I'd just had was still vivid. Perhaps it hadn't been a dream.
Bzzzzzt.
I heard the crackle of dissipating electricity, and Bihyung vanished without a word. He'd probably gone off to do his own work.
Somehow, I breathed a sigh of relief.
A Stream Contract with a dokkaebi.
It was a gamble I could never have attempted if I hadn't learned about Bihyung from ‘Ways of Survival.’
But I'd pulled it off, with an almost uncanny composure.
Me, who couldn't land even a modest contract in actual ‘reality.’
[The exclusive skill, ‘Fourth Wall,’ is active.]
······Reality, huh.
I tightened my right hand around the thorn.
Did I really think of this world as reality?
[A few constellations want you to act quickly.]
Well, this wasn't the time to sit around pondering things like that.
I swung the thorn with all my might and smashed through the stomach wall, which had lost its elasticity.
With a rumbling crash, it collapsed and water poured in. I plunged into the Han River.
“Phaa!”
Fortunately, there were no other ichthyosaurs in sight. I saw small sea-beast species approaching curiously, but sensed no particular hostility. Not all monsters attack humans.
Was Dongho Bridge over there?
Using a floating chunk of the ichthyosaur's corpse as an inner tube, I kicked clumsily toward shore.
The cold water stung my skin, but this wasn't the time to worry about that. After swimming like that for about 30 minutes, my hand touched the shore.
[A few constellations grow tense as they watch you.]
Usually, danger struck immediately after a message like this appeared.
[The constellation, ‘Abyssal Black Flame Dragon,’ gives a sinister smile.]
Too bad for the constellations who disliked me, but that wasn't going to happen.
I already knew what danger was coming.
[You have entered the second main scenario area.]
[The ground in this scenario area is severely contaminated.]
[Hold your breath and move underground as quickly as possible.]
That was how the message explained it, but in fact, you weren't supposed to be aboveground from the moment this scenario began.
Why? One look at my skin would tell you.
[You have been exposed to highly poisonous fog.]
The skin touched by the purple fog was turning black.
Gyaaaaaah!
Following the fog toward its source, I saw a monstrous beast letting out a terrible cry.
An enormous monster standing well over thirty meters tall.
This fog was the fart of a grade-7 monstrous beast, a ‘Corpse-Poison Rhinoceros.’
The rhinoceros was snorting as it confronted a monstrous beast beyond the fog. From the shadow I glimpsed, it seemed to be an insect-king species (蟲王種).
Graaaaaah······.
Humans weren't the only ones struggling in this new world.
The monstrous beasts, too, were fighting for their own territory.
I moved while holding my breath as long as I could.

They were grade-7 monstrous beasts like the ichthyosaur, but they weren't creatures I could take on right now. I'd only been able to kill the Sea Commander because I'd made the necessary preparations.
[Using ‘Ellain Monkey’s Lungs.’]
The monkey's lungs were an item that could serve as a substitute for an air purifier for 20 minutes. I'd bought them from Bihyung in advance.
[A few constellations marvel at your preparedness!]
Oksu Station, which was aboveground, had already been destroyed.
The nearest ‘underground station’ was Geumho Station.
The others had probably all moved there, too.
I hurried along the side of the road, avoiding the small species tearing into the corpses. I had only 20 minutes, so I needed to gather daily necessities as quickly as possible before moving on.
First, I needed clothes.
The ichthyosaur's digestive fluid had dissolved my outer clothing, so I needed something to wear. Of course, there were things to wear scattered all around. It was just an unpleasant prospect.
······I supposed I'd have to make do.
I searched the corpses, picked out a few roughly fitting pieces of clothing and put them on, then headed straight for a nearby convenience store.
I grabbed several plastic bags and indiscriminately swept compact, dense foods into them.
The food would make useful trading goods once I went underground.
I'd filled about three or four bags when I noticed the monkey's lungs in my mouth gradually turning black.
Not much time left now.
That was when I heard someone's voice.
“H-help······ please help me.”
Someone was still alive?
A young woman lay collapsed in a corner, curled up.
The contamination was spreading across her skin, but the poisoning wasn't severe because she was wearing a mask she'd had on hand.
I didn't know what she'd been through, but her top was half stripped off and some of the stitching in her skirt had been torn.
“Are you all right? Can you stand?”
“Uuuuugh······.”
Had there been an extra like her in ‘Ways of Survival’? I wanted to take a closer look, but there wasn't time. I hoisted her onto my back and ran toward Geumho Station.
Rounding the corner along the roadside, I came straight to the main road. Geumho Station was now a hundred meters away in a straight line.
I drew a sharp breath and began sprinting down the main road at full speed.
The sign for Exit 3, visible in the distance.
······Closed.
Then what about the other side?
Perhaps because of the disaster, the fire shutters were down at every exit. I could break through a shutter with the thorn, but if I wasn't careful, the people inside could get hurt.
“Exit 4, Exit 4······.”

Unexpectedly, the woman on my back proved helpful. I ran toward Exit 4 and spotted its fire shutter coming down just then. I jammed the thorn into the gap beneath the closing shutter. Someone shouted.
“Fuck, what the hell!”
“Open the door.”
“N-no! You can't come in! Get back!”
“I have an injured person here.”
“We're already at capacity! We don't need anyone else!”
They weren't letting anyone in because they were at capacity?
Strange. Had that happened in the story?
“That's none of my business.”

I wedged the thorn in as a lever and lifted the shutter with all my strength. I'd also used the coins I'd earned to raise my Strength to level 10, so I could now exert the monstrous strength of five or six grown men or more.
“Waaaaagh!”
With a crash, the people lowering the shutter from the other side went sprawling.
“R-run!”
The frightened men fled into the darkness of the underground passage. Having made it safely into the station, I lowered the shutter and laid the woman on the floor.
[You have entered a safe area.]
The highly poisonous fog didn't reach underground. There wasn't really a scientific explanation for it. It was simply because of the ‘scenario.’
“Hold this in your mouth.”
I removed the woman's mask and put the monkey's lungs I'd been holding in my own mouth into hers. It probably wouldn't cure her completely, but it should at least have a neutralizing effect.
A faint groan escaped the woman's lips.
The woman who'd been abandoned.
I suddenly grew curious about her information. If events had followed the original story, this woman, too, would most likely have died there.
Just as I was about to activate ‘Character List,’ I heard a voice.
“That's him over there!”
A flashlight beam gleamed in the darkness as it drew closer.
Squinting, I could dimly make out men, each holding something like an iron pipe.
[The constellation, ‘Prisoner of the Golden Headband,’ frowns at the arrival of the uninvited guests.]
The large man in the middle spoke. Judging by his well-proportioned build, he was definitely a fellow with some muscle.
“What the hell are you?”
Strangely, I found myself at a loss for words.
What was I supposed to say at a time like this? After thinking for a moment, I tried speaking like Yoo Joonghyuk.
“Kim Dokja.”
“······Kim Dokja? Is that your name?”
“Yeah.”
“Who asked you that! I'm asking what the fuck you do!”
An even more troublesome question came back.
“H-hey! That woman······.”
One of the men spotted the woman lying beside me and shone his flashlight on her.
“What the hell, isn't she from the marginalized group? Didn't she come back with you?”
“W-well, that's······.”
The man's flashlight moved around the woman's waist as though fondling her.
“···Ha, so that's what happened. Cute little bastards. Who said you could run a little sideline without your hyung-nim's permission?”
“H-heh. Sorry.”
“O-of course, Cheolsoo hyung-nim would go first······ Hehe, that was what we intended.”
Cheolsoo? Cheolsoo, huh. Had there been a character with that name? The fact that I couldn't remember meant he was a nobody despite his appearance.
“Hey, hand that woman over to us······ Huh? What's that?”
The flashlight beam settled on the convenience-store bags on the floor.
It was good that I'd escaped the danger, but somehow, things weren't heading in a good direction.
“Leave that too, and get the fuck outside. Then I'll let you live.”
To be precise, I meant things weren't heading in a good direction for those men, not for me.
[The constellation, ‘Prisoner of the Golden Headband,’ is irritated by the appearance of the small fry.]
[The constellation, ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire,’ is enraged by the injustice before it.]
[A bounty scenario has been generated at the constellations' request!]
<Bounty Scenario – Remove the Interference>
Category : Sub
Difficulty : F
Clear Conditions : The constellations are greatly angered by the appearance of nuisances who are impeding the rapid progression of events. Incapacitate them within the time limit.
Time Limit : 5 minutes
Reward : ???
Failure : ???
I knew this would happen. Poor bastards.
I gripped the thorn and stood up.
There weren't any minors among the constellations, were there?
I trusted there weren't.
Because from this point on, the broadcast was adults-only.
Sometimes, I wondered.
Why did so many post-apocalyptic stories feature ‘predictable villains’?
Wasn't it lazy of writers to assume crimes like rape and theft would run rampant even in such circumstances?
Perhaps if the world's actual ‘end’ came, humans would behave more rationally than expected.
“Looks like he isn't leaving. Hey, go kill him!”
The answer was right in front of me now.
The men inching toward me warily, and the man behind them watching as though enjoying a spectacle.
[The constellation, ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire,’ anticipates a just judgment.]
It struck me anew.
Human imagination was trite, and actual humans were even more trite than that imagination.
Whoosh!
An iron pipe swept clumsily through the air. It wasn't a blow with any killing intent behind it. In fact, even if it had hit me, it would hardly have hurt.
“I-if you don't run, you'll really die. Get lost!”
Four men had surrounded me. One was trembling, but they all looked more at ease than before. Probably because there were more of them now.
“What are you doing, you bastards!”
With a shout of “Waaaaah!” one of the men charged. His stance was so unguarded it was almost pitiful. I moved the thorn.
Shunk!
“Aaaaaagh! My leg! My leg!”
“You son of a bitch!”
“Get him, all at once!”
The agitated men charged one after another, but I wasn't afraid.
Their Strength levels barely exceeded 5. Taking every blow that rained down on me, I silently thrust the thorn.
Bang! Clang!
Shunk! Shunk!
Their thighs pierced one after another, the men screamed and fell to their knees.
But I didn't kill them. The scenario's clear conditions specified ‘incapacitation,’ after all.
[Constellations aligned with Absolute Good (絕對善) nod at your decision.]
[A few constellations mock your humanity.]
[The constellations have sponsored you with 100 coins.]
Becoming a bloodthirsty killer might draw the constellations' interest for a while, but only for a while. Raising their threshold for stimulation all at once wouldn't be good in the long run.
[3 minutes remain until the sub-scenario ends.]
Two minutes so far.
Keeping track of time mattered in a time attack.
“W-what the hell is with this bastard! Why won't he die?”
At that point, the leader, who'd been watching from the rear, stepped forward.
“So you can take a beating. Everyone, stand back. I'll handle him.”
“Cheolsoo hyung-nim! I think that bastard has a constellation sponsor!”
“Good. He looks like he's got plenty of coins.”
Knuckle dusters gleaming with a black sheen. They weren't ordinary iron knuckle dusters.
Was this fellow backed by a constellation sponsor?
Crack.
The joints cracked as the man flexed the hand wearing the knuckle dusters.
[The character ‘Bang Cheolsoo’ has used ‘Threaten.’]
[The disparity in overall stats is too great for ‘Threaten’ to take effect.]
“Oh, you've got some guts, huh? You're not scared at all.”
Before he even finished speaking, the man's fist moved. An attack aimed squarely at my jaw. I quickly took a couple of steps back. He grinned.
“Not bad. You've done some training, huh?”

Anyone could manage this with Agility above level 10, even without a special footwork skill. I'd invested most of the coins left after buying items in my stats, bringing the combined levels of my Constitution, Strength, and Agility to 33.
Now, how about we see what this fellow's got?
[Activating the exclusive skill ‘Character List’!]
<Character Information>
Name : Bang Cheolsoo
Age : 34
Constellation Sponsor (背後星) : Monarch of the Small Fries
Exclusive Attribute : Assault Force Captain (General)
Exclusive Skills : [Dogfight Lv.2], [Bluff Lv.2]
Stigma : [Threaten Lv.1]
Overall Stats : [Constitution Lv.6], [Strength Lv.7], [Agility Lv.6], [Magic Power Lv.2]
Overall Evaluation : An ordinary thug who was lucky enough to obtain a constellation sponsor. He tends to overestimate his abilities relative to his actual combat power.
Ah······ I see. Now I remembered.
“Bang Cheolsoo of the Cheoldoo Group.”
“What, you know me?”
“Who knows?”
They'd appeared like the wind early in the story and vanished like the wind, so my memory was hazy. But there had definitely been a character named ‘Bang Cheolsoo.’
He'd been the biggest idiot among the people in Geumho Station's ‘group.’
As far as I knew, these men should originally have been beaten to death by Yoo Joonghyuk. Why were they still alive?
“Oho, are you one of ‘those’ types too? Looks like you've killed your share of people. Right? Somehow, you feel like a kindred spirit.”
[The character ‘Bang Cheolsoo’ has activated ‘Bluff.’]
Bluff. A skill any thug worth a damn possessed. It was a good debuff that could dampen the combat power of a mentally weak opponent, but this case was different.
[‘Fourth Wall’ blocks the Bluff of the character ‘Bang Cheolsoo’.]
[The confidence of the character ‘Bang Cheolsoo’ plummets.]
“Ignoring me? You must really want to fucking die.”
Taking a Greco-Roman wrestling stance, Bang Cheolsoo radiated menace, as though ready to lunge at me at any moment. But that, too, was all bluff.
Because he didn't have the [Wrestling] skill.
“Quit making a fool of yourself and come at me.”
“You bastard!”
His main skill was level-2 [Dogfight].
As long as it didn't turn into a wild brawl, his combat power was negligible.
“Die!”
Perhaps because of the large gap in Agility, his attacks rarely connected.
I looked at him with something like pity.
Not every constellation wanted to raise its incarnation into the scenario's ‘protagonist.’
For instance, his constellation, ‘Monarch of the Small Fries,’ was famous for not caring about its incarnation.
A masochist who simply chose an idiot it could push around and toy with as its incarnation, then enjoyed watching that incarnation get wrecked by other incarnations.
That was ‘Monarch of the Small Fries.’
[The constellation, ‘Monarch of the Small Fries,’ is enjoying this.]
[The constellation, ‘Monarch of the Small Fries,’ has sponsored you with 100 coins.]
It even cheered for the enemy when its own incarnation was about to be crushed.
Originally, I'd intended to put him down with a single blow because of the time limit, but this changed things a little.
[2 minutes remain until the sub-scenario ends.]
Then how about putting the remaining time to the best possible use?
“You little rat!”
Even his lines were all in the style of ‘Monarch of the Small Fries.’ Poor fellow.
Thwack!
“Haha! Got you!”
His attack connected by luck, but naturally, it did almost no damage. The spot he'd hit only stung a little.
“How!”
What did he mean, how? My Constitution was level 12 now. His Strength was only level 7. A difference in the leading digit of a stat created a huge disparity in combat power.
“My turn now, right?”
I gave the stunned Bang Cheolsoo a couple of light taps on the cheek, then struck his face with all my might. A couple of teeth flew out at once, and he screamed as he went sprawling.
Then, without hesitation, I raised the thorn and drove it straight through his arm.
“Aaaaaagh!”

After pinning one of his arms to the wall with the thorn, I began beating him mercilessly. His back, thighs, upper thighs, and sides—I picked only the places where it would hurt most without knocking him out in a single blow.
[The constellation, ‘Monarch of the Small Fries,’ is enjoying this.]
[The constellation, ‘Monarch of the Small Fries,’ has requested an extension of the sub-scenario's time limit.]
[The sub-scenario is extended by 1 minute.]
I also used the woman's injuries as a guide.
“Guh! Kgh! Ghuuugh!”
Blood flew, and flesh flew. Broken teeth rolled across the floor, and broken joints bent into grotesque shapes. Still, I didn't stop kicking.
“S-stop! Please! Let our hyung-nim go!”
The men nearby shouted in panic. I looked at each of them in turn. Then I looked at the woman lying on the floor, half stripped of her clothes.
Humans were weak.
How could such weak humans commit acts this cruel? With nothing but the excuse that the world had ended. Killing other people, raping women, taking what belonged to others.
Because of instinct?
Looking into Bang Cheolsoo's eyes, stained with fear in the face of greater violence, I suddenly grew curious.
“Why did you do it?”
It was a question without context.
So it wasn't a question I expected an answer to. But just as I was about to kick him again, Bang Cheolsoo opened his eyes wide.
“Fuuuuck······ Just kill me, you son of a bitch.”
The moment I saw those eyes, I knew he'd answered my question in his own way. Eyes with no lingering attachment to life. I see. So it hadn't been instinct.
In a fading voice, Bang Cheolsoo babbled.
“This fucking, fucking world······.”
He was the sort of person who'd been steeped in despair long before this world fell to ruin. Just like me.
[10 seconds remain until the sub-scenario ends.]
Without further delay, I delivered a powerful kick to his neck.
With a choking gasp, Bang Cheolsoo finally passed out.
[The sub-scenario's clear conditions have been met.]
[You have obtained 300 coins.]
That ought to have satisfied the bastard.
[The constellation, ‘Monarch of the Small Fries,’ is satisfied and has sponsored you with an additional 100 coins.]
One by one, the men approached, practically crawling across the floor.
“H-how could you be so cruel······.”
After examining Bang Cheolsoo, who'd been reduced to a ragged wreck, they looked up at me without daring to open their mouths. Like dogs in a slaughterhouse waiting to learn their fate.
I hoisted the collapsed woman onto my back and picked up the convenience-store bags.
Whatever the case, the world had ended, and I had to get on with a new everyday life.
“Take me to where the group is.”
Originally, Geumho Station had grown into a local stronghold after Yoo Joonghyuk cleaned it up.
In his first regression, Yoo Joonghyuk had made it through the second main scenario with the Geumho Station group, which had allowed its members to each claim a place for themselves in the new age.
But that was the first round. The Yoo Joonghyuk of the third regression was different.
The third-round Yoo Joonghyuk had been born a monster who monopolized everything.
“······Even so, he used to at least clean things up before leaving.”
“Pardon?”
The man guiding me asked, startled.
“Just talking to myself. It's a habit.”
[The constellation, ‘Secretive Plotter,’ likes your self-talk.]
“Yeees······ Anyway, this way.”
The men of the Cheoldoo Group, who'd been supporting one another, stopped. Descending below the unlit platform, I found an area that still had electricity.
As soon as we descended past the landing, I heard people murmuring.
“It's the Cheoldoo Group! Someone's hurt!”
Several people hurried over to support Bang Cheolsoo and his men. They seemed more organized than I'd expected, moving in perfect coordination.
Then I saw familiar faces running toward me.
“Oh my goodness. Dokja-ssi! Kim Dokja-ssi!”
Fortunately, it seemed nothing serious had happened to them.
“Yoo Sangah-ssi.”
“I'm so relieved. I'm really, really relieved!”
Yoo Sangah stood before me, looking as though she didn't know what to do. I awkwardly offered the astonished Yoo Sangah a handshake.
There were little scratches on the backs of her hands. She seemed to have been through quite a lot over the past four days.
Just then, I heard a soft thump, and something clung to my leg.
“So you're alive.”
Lee Gilyoung. I stroked the boy's head.
“Have you been all right?”
Lee Gilyoung nodded. His cheeks were sunken—he must have gone terribly hungry. I took a chocolate bar from a bag and put it in his hand.
“You really are alive, Dokja-ssi. Hah······.”
Lee Hyunsung was the last to reach me. His upper-body muscles had grown firmer, as though he'd developed a little in the meantime. He'd probably been protecting the other two.
“I'm truly sorry. For leaving you behind then, Dokja-ssi······.”
“There was nothing you could do in that situation.”
“Whew, thank goodness Yoo Joonghyuk-ssi was right.”
······Yoo Joonghyuk? Why was that name coming up here?
Lee Hyunsung hesitated, gauging my reaction, then spoke.
“Well, Yoo Joonghyuk-ssi said you were probably alive, Kim Dokja-ssi······.”
“······Where is Yoo Joonghyuk now?”
“Well, he isn't here at the moment.”
He wasn't here?
“Yoo Joonghyuk-ssi left the station yesterday. So······.”
Before Lee Hyunsung even finished, I understood several things.
I see.
So that was what had happened after all.
Always in such a hurry, that bastard.
“Come to think of it, someone else is missing too.”
“Oh, the department head······.”
Yoo Sangah couldn't continue because some men suddenly barged in. But in the end, that worked out well.
“Everyone, move!”

Because I could tell immediately what had happened without hearing an explanation. Three or four men, each armed with tools such as hammers or pipes, began surrounding me as though making a show of force.
And a familiar face at their center.
Han Myungoh, who'd abandoned me and run off at the Even Bridge, looked as though he'd seen a ghost. As expected, he seemed to have attached himself to that group.
“G-get that bastard out. He's vicious! He shouldn't be here!”
His guilty conscience getting the better of him, Han Myungoh began making a fuss, perhaps thinking I would take revenge.
But the men merely exchanged glances, reluctant to move.
Something felt strange.
They had Han Myungoh at their center, but weren't listening to him?
“Haha, Han hyung. We should all get along. What's the matter?”
“Ah, w-well.”
“You must be our new arrival today.”
The men parted to either side, opening a path.
A slender man emerging from the crowd.
One look at his eyes told me.
As expected, he had a constellation sponsor.
“A pleasure to meet you. May I ask your name?”
“I'm Kim Dokja.”
“Kim Dokja-ssi. I see. My name is Cheon Inho.”
Cheon Inho? A name I felt I might remember.
I tightened my grip on the thorn.
From the look of things, the men of the Cheoldoo Group were under his command.
Since I'd beaten them half to hell, it was only natural that he would pick a fight with me.
“I've heard all about it from the people who came with you. You fought monsters and saved our group members, I hear.”
“Everyone, please gather round! We have a brave new group member here!”
At Cheon Inho's words, people began peering over one by one.
Of course. Han Myungoh's charisma could never have brought together a force this size. This fellow was the crowd's real leader.
“Wow! That's food!”
The hungry people's eyes fixed on the convenience-store bags. Cheon Inho spoke as though he'd been waiting for that moment.
“He says he personally went and got it for us. Such a good man is a rare find.”
At those words, their gazes fixed on me as though I were their savior.
A mother holding a child, an elderly person with an injured leg—they were all looking at me with desperate eyes.
Cheon Inho······ I thought I might remember.
Yes, he'd been in the Geumho Station group.
[The constellation, ‘Secretive Plotter,’ grows excited.]
In a ruined world, the truly dangerous people weren't men like Bang Cheolsoo. People lashing out in despair weren't dangerous at all.
The truly dangerous ones were those who used other people's despair as fertilizer for their power. Just like this fellow.
“Welcome to Geumho Station, Kim Dokja-ssi.”
Cheon Inho's eyes smiled deeply as they met mine. Accepting his offered handshake, I smiled inwardly.
Cheon Inho wouldn't know.
That his future had been decided at this very moment.
Despite Cheon Inho's antics, the constellations didn't request a ‘bounty scenario.’
Meaning this wasn't yet the best time to deal with him.
For about half a day after that, I focused on learning the situation at Geumho Station. Most of my information came from Lee Hyunsung.
“There are currently 86 people gathered at Geumho Station. Ah, including you, Dokja-ssi, that makes 87 now.”
“Fewer than I expected.”
“Yes. Only the people near the station and on the trains when the scenario broke out survived. Nobody talks about it, but they probably all, in the first scenario······.”
I knew the rest without him saying it. Their expressions alone told me. People who'd survived by trampling on someone else's life. Everyone here was a murderer.
“Geumho Station is currently divided into two main groups. Strictly speaking, it's one group and everyone else.”
Lee Hyunsung looked toward the people, his expression dark. Men armed with iron pipes or tools. It was obvious at a glance which side was the mainstream.
“Just trust me! The chairman of the conglomerate is working on it, so you'll all be rescued soon.”
Department Head Han Myungoh, the youngest son of the Hankyung Group family.
“Hyung-nim is right, everyone. Don't lose hope. We can get out.”
And Cheon Inho, the power behind the scenes who'd taken Han Myungoh under his wing and was actually leading the group. They were presumably the ‘mainstream group.’
“I'm bored, Mom······ Can't I play a game on the phone?”
“Be patient a little longer. The rescue team will be here soon.”
“I'm telling you, the government will act. A country doesn't collapse that easily.”
And the remaining people, collectively called the ‘marginalized group,’ were scraping together a living under the mainstream group's protection.

They seemed far too weak-willed to have killed anyone. But even among a hundred murderers, there would be strong and weak. Perhaps they didn't think of themselves as murderers. They believed it had all been unavoidable.
Looking toward the mainstream group stirring up the people, Lee Hyunsung spoke.
“The mainstream group decides how food is distributed. They've already cleared out the convenience stores and restaurants in the station······ and the food we can eat right away is almost gone.”
“I see.”
“Because of that, since yesterday, the mainstream group has been selecting people to send aboveground to search for food. Heewon-ssi, who'd been staying with us, was one of those selected.”
“Heewon-ssi······?”
“Ah, that's the name of the woman you rescued earlier today, Dokja-ssi.”
I looked at the woman lying on a subway bench.
